It does not appropriately capture the risk related to the Gen-AI enabled software
function.As a resident physician in the psychiatry space, it is imperative that we
are able to define clear and objective methods for the risk of the anything medical
advice made. Clearly we have always had several cases of issues and court
cases where the generativeAI is indicated and gave false information.
positions.position_gist: The two-axis risk framework does not adequately capture risk; clearer, more objective methods for assessing the risk of any medical advice are needed, given documented cases of generative AI providing false information.

positions.position_gist: Action-directing functions should carry an explicit warning message whenever any medical knowledge or guidance is involved, directed not only at physicians but also therapists, counselors, and hotline staff, reinforcing that human mental health professionals should be used rather than AI models.

positions.source_passage:
Manufactures can put their disclaimer, but in the end, anyone that
participates in the use of AI in this space bares reasonability. The government system
itself, no one is immune to the consequences that will come with it. There are no
acceptable trade-offs by a clinical context. As a physician the oath comes into play: do
no harm, and since right now AI carries more risk and more reasonability
positions.position_gist: There are no acceptable escalation-error trade-offs by clinical context; manufacturer disclaimers do not remove responsibility, which falls on everyone who participates in using AI, and current AI carries more risk than benefit under the do-no-harm obligation.

positions.source_passage:
The approach seems ideal in hindsight, but how will one maintain patient
safety and data during this? Who is not to say that the data gets leaked anyway, and in
that case who is responsible?
positions.position_gist: The competency-based approach seems appealing in principle but the commenter questions how patient safety and data will be protected during it and who bears responsibility if data are leaked.

positions.source_passage:
The two-axis framework is not even needed. Currently HIPPA laws and the
Security Rule of Healthcare govern that all healthcare providers within the space must
follow the same privacy and security that all would want--- how will the FDA,
government, manufactures, and physicians and other healthcare colleagues ensure that
patient data will be protected and not breached or stolen or sold?
positions.position_gist: The two-axis framework is unnecessary given existing HIPAA and Security Rule obligations, and the central unanswered question is how FDA, manufacturers, and clinicians will ensure patient data is not breached, stolen, or sold.

positions.source_passage:
The benchmarking structure is nice, but a clinical trial or study would need to
be done and the idea of informed consent would have to be discussed. In essence as
well how does that maintain that patient confidentiality will be paramount while
delivering accurate and clinically appropriate data/info?
positions.position_gist: Benchmarking alone is insufficient—a clinical trial or study plus explicit treatment of informed consent and patient confidentiality is needed.

positions.position_gist: The benchmarking concept needs further development and validation through a clearly specified pilot study, including a dedicated behavioral health study given that field's nuance and higher consequences, with accountability for patient safety and informed consent clarified.
